clue.text: Man's in a place that's seedy and tacky

indicators.note: the man's contribution sits inside the seedy place, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club

explanation.surface: A rundown man about town is described as living somewhere seedy and cheap-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacky' wants to mean tasteless, matching 'seedy'; here it means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacky is slightly sticky, and an adhesive is a substance or surface that sticks.

clue.text: In search of peace, hail soothing application

explanation.surface: A troubled soul seeking peace salutes a calming balm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In search of' supplies letters itself rather than being a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a lotion applied to the face to soothe the skin after shaving.

clue.text: Bowler maybe demands pardon after dismissing opener

indicators.note: dismissing the opener sends the first batter off, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: What? asks for a remark to be repeated

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler appeals for a decision once the opening batter is out.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words point to a player; the bowler is a hat, the bowler being a hard round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a type of hat, so 'maybe' marks it as one example of headwear.

clue.text: Spread betting not ordained by boss to run daily?

parts.note: starting price, the odds at the off
the editor runs the daily paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor launches a daily column on spread betting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread betting' is a real phrase, but 'Spread' alone is the definition; SP is the starting price in horse-race betting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something splayed is spread out or opened wide, like splayed fingers.

clue.text: Leg disfigured with a love bite — the product of rape?

definitions.note: rape here is the oilseed plant

indicators.note: disfigured means spoiled in shape, so these letters lose their original order

explanation.surface: A grim question about bruises; the surface is deliberately shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: Rape is also oilseed rape, the yellow-flowered crop grown for its oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil pressed from rapeseed is a plant-derived cooking oil, the crop's main product.

clue.text: Things dropped from the bloom a bush regularly displayed

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the phrase is shown

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A gardener watches petals falling from a flowering shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden picture makes 'Things dropped' sound like petals; the things are bombs dropped from aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen bombs are weapons delivered by being released from an aircraft over a target.

clue.text: One's not prone to fail in such a position?

definitions.text: One's not prone to fail in such a position?

parts.note: surface reading: someone not inclined to failure
setter's reading: lying face up rather than face down, the position of a dead fish, and to go so is to fail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' looks like 'inclined to'; it means lying face down, and someone not prone lies face up.
explanation.definitionFit: To go belly-up is an idiom for a business failing, from a dead fish floating on its back.

clue.text: Academic rose, condemning boxing in an instant

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the clue's own words hold the answer inside them like a box

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the three words, ignoring the comma and spaces

explanation.surface: A don stands up to speak out against the sport of boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like the sport being condemned; it is the instruction to look inside the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A microsecond is a millionth of a second, a tiny span of time, so it serves as a synonym for an instant.

clue.text: Put up with foot of slime? It's more than an inch

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high in the air

explanation.surface: A slug leaves a long trail of slime after crawling some distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island; Skye is a large island of the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a big Scottish island, so more than a mere inch, the Scots name for an islet.

clue.text: Returning for one drink, we don't approve of this charge

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the run of pieces is read from the end

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at a drinks surcharge on a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a fee; it is the care of a guardian, as in a child in your charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is guardianship, and someone in your charge is under your tutelage.

clue.text: In pursuit of cup, ultimately happy with bottle

indicators.note: something in pursuit follows behind, so this piece is placed after the other
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word before is kept

explanation.surface: A cup-winning team is happy with the bottle of champagne they receive.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve or courage, so 'with bottle' means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means showing courage, the quality the British call bottle.

clue.text: Sweets are enticements to come round grandmother's place

indicators.note: to come round something is to surround it, so the enticements enclose the place

parts.note: nana is a pet name for a grandmother
standard abbreviation, as in street names

explanation.surface: Children are coaxed round to Granny's with promises of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain sweets also means desserts, puddings, not only candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is a dessert of a halved banana with ice cream, and sweets is a British word for desserts.

clue.text: Firm to attempt to chase money order for competitors

indicators.note: something chasing comes behind, so these pieces follow the money

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A company tries to recover a payment instruction on behalf of rival businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a money order; it is a command, the starter's call at a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional starting command given to racers, telling them when to set off.

clue.text: Article serving as clothing for a day, dressing down

indicators.note: clothing wraps around a body, so the serving word is wrapped around the day

parts.note: end of dishing, as in dishing up

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on wearing casual clothes for a day: dress-down Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing down' looks like casual wear; here it is a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down is a severe scolding, and admonishing someone is reprimanding them.

clue.text: Fifties Times cutting collected for retail deadline?

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so these pieces split the word for collected

parts.note: as in three by four, multiplied

explanation.surface: A cutting from The Times in the fifties, gathered for a shop's closing date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' means calm and composed, SEDATE, not gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-by date is the last day a shop may sell a product, a deadline for retail.

clue.text: Close passport, for example, having dislodged page in sulk

indicators.note: dislodging pushes something out of its spot and takes it, so one letter is swapped for the passport piece

parts.note: a passport is a form of identification
to have the hump is to sulk

explanation.surface: Someone sulking shuts their passport after a page has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb about the passport; it is the adjective for muggy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is warm, damp and airless, which is what humid describes.

clue.text: During rap, female overcomes pressure to swear

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the rest sits inside the rap

parts.note: take the rap means take the blame

indicators.note: to overcome is taken as to come over and cover, so the female surrounds pressure

explanation.surface: A woman rapper pushes past the pressure to put swear words in her lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' sounds like the music; it is blame, as in taking the rap.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to speak profanely or curse, which is one sense of swearing.

clue.text: Euro zone initially put in place by the French, Italian or Spanish state

indicators.note: by means beside, so the French article is placed alongside
putting something in a place means it goes inside, so these letters go within the venue

parts.note: a place where an event happens

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the euro and zone are used

explanation.surface: A news line about which European state is placed inside the euro zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a country in Europe; the state is South American, its name meaning 'little Venice' in Italian, and it is Spanish-speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Venezuela's name is an Italian coinage and its people speak Spanish, so it is a state with both connections.

clue.text: Fellow guarded with zeal every second having previously escaped

indicators.note: previously means earlier, so this piece is placed before the other
with every second letter gone, only the first and third of the four survive

explanation.surface: A man held in custody with keen guards escapes anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escaped' completes the letter selection: every second letter has escaped from zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name stands for a fellow, a common crossword convention.

clue.text: Where you'll find stem — and large stalk

parts.note: the stem is the timber at the very front of a ship, at its bow

explanation.surface: A gardener's riddle about where to find a plant stem on a big stalk.
explanation.walkthrough: Stem and stalk look like botany; the stem is part of a ship and the stalk is hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk prey is to move stealthily after it, which is what prowling means.

clue.text: Short trousers incorporating design that's something ornamental

indicators.note: incorporating means taking inside, so the design word goes within
short means cut off, so the last letter of the trousers word is removed

parts.note: an aim or purpose, as in to that end

explanation.surface: Shorts with a pattern sewn in, worn as a decorative item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short trousers' looks like a single item; 'Short' is an instruction and 'design' means intention.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a decorative item hanging from a chain, an ornament.

clue.text: Occasion of speech by King's son is dynastic PR, outrageously

indicators.note: acting outrageously means behaving wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: letters rearranged together with the I and S of 'is'

explanation.surface: A royal heir's speech is dismissed as shameless publicity for the dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry V the King rallies his troops before Agincourt on St Crispin's Day; the 'is' joins the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V's famous 'band of brothers' speech is set on that saint's feast day, 25 October.

clue.text: Cover live sports

indicators.note: sports is read as the verb meaning plays about, so the letters frolic into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcaster covers live sporting events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover live sports' reads as broadcasting; 'sports' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a piece of fabric that conceals, and to veil is to hide.

clue.text: In retrospect, judge one visits fit to be a prophet

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so these letters go within the word for fit
retrospect is looking back, so the whole result is read backwards

explanation.surface: Looking back, a judge decides someone is fit to be a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit is HALE, healthy; J and I go inside it before the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is an Old Testament prophet from the Books of Kings.

clue.text: I'm obliged, half the time, to enter by way of compound

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these pieces go into the words for by way of
half means only part is used, so the second three letters of the time word are dropped

explanation.surface: Someone grateful must pass through a walled compound only half the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like an enclosure to enter; it is a chemical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin A, retinol, is an organic chemical compound needed in the diet.

clue.text: Some number subtracted from precise set of cubes?

indicators.note: subtracting takes something away, so one letter comes out of the word for precise

parts.note: n, an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A maths problem about taking a number away from a set of cubes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cubes' suggests geometry or dice; ice cubes are meant, set as in frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice comes in cubes, and frozen water has set solid, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Extra's so long on stage

indicators.note: on means attached after, so the farewell is placed behind the stage

parts.note: a stage of a journey is a leg

explanation.surface: A film extra says farewell after a part in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a leg bye is a run scored off the batter's body, counted as an extra rather than to the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are cricket runs not credited to a batter, and a leg bye is one kind of them.

clue.text: One might say grace at last, after waiter's moved

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted from their places into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with its s

indicators.note: at last means at the end, so only the final letter of grace is taken

explanation.surface: Someone says grace at the end of a meal once the waiter has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One might say grace' reads as a single phrase; the definition stops at 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is a hedging phrase meaning so to speak, the way one might put it.
